title: Four Floating Sauna Myths
why: Cold-audience myth bust: removes the four reasons Portlanders hesitate (plunge pressure, rain, party vibe, experience).
hook_options: Four things people assume about a floating sauna.
You don't have to jump in. And three more.
Most of what you've heard is wrong, in a good way.
caption: Four things people assume before their first session. You don't have to plunge, rain helps, it's calm not loud, and nobody needs experience. Heat, cold, rest, repeat. #EbbAndEmber #PortlandSauna #FloatingSauna #ColumbiaRiver

slides.headline: Four things people assume about a floating sauna.
slides.body: Most of them are wrong in a way that's good news.

slides.headline: You have to plunge in the river.
slides.body: The river part scares off a lot of people.

slides.headline: The plunge is optional. Always.
slides.body: There's a cold shower on deck. Some guests never touch the river and leave happy.

slides.headline: Rain ruins the session.
slides.body: Portland forecast says rain, so people reschedule.

slides.headline: Rain makes the heat better.
slides.body: Gray sky, flat water, rain on the windows, 180 degrees on the bench. Best seat in Portland weather.

slides.headline: Social, not loud.
slides.body: Up to 8 guests in a social session. Think campfire conversation, not rooftop bar.

slides.headline: You need sauna experience.
slides.body: People worry they'll do it wrong.

slides.headline: First-timers do fine here.
slides.body: The routine is heat, cold, rest, repeat. Clear signs walk you from the parking lot to the dock.

slides.headline: Now come see for yourself.
slides.body: Book a session on the Columbia at ebbandember.com.
